current_disclosures.section: Results of Operations > Operating Income by Reportable Segments
current_disclosures.summary: The year-on-year decrease in All Other operating loss was attributed to the absence of the $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost incurred in fiscal year 2023, partially offset by an $839 million increase in stock-based compensation expense in fiscal year 2024.

materiality_analysis.reason: The prior year's operating expenses were heavily distorted by a $1.35–$1.4 billion one-time Arm acquisition termination charge. The current year reports 'organic' expense growth driven by employees and compensation, providing a clearer picture of ongoing operational spending and profitability.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Exclusion of one-time acquisition termination charge from operating expense baseline

current_disclosures.summary: Operating expenses increased 45% year-over-year, driven by higher compensation and benefits costs from employee growth and increases, as well as higher engineering development, compute, and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure introduces specific drivers for operating expense growth, explicitly adding 'engineering development, compute, and infrastructure costs for new product introductions' as a key factor alongside compensation. This signals a shift in cost structure towards R&D and compute infrastructure, which is a meaningful operational change compared to the previous year's focus on general employee growth and compensation.

comparisons.peer_topic: All Other operating loss breakdown for 2024 and 2023
comparisons.peer_summary: All Other operating loss was $4.2 billion in 2024 and $4.4 billion in 2023, primarily consisting of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and stock-based compensation expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD discuss the composition and drivers of their 'Other' operating expenses or losses. NVDA highlights that operating expenses increased in 2024 due to employee growth and compensation, contrasting with a significant one-time charge in the prior year. Similarly, AMD breaks down its 'All Other operating loss,' noting it primarily consisted of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and stock-based compensation expense. While NVDA focuses on the year-over-year increase in personnel costs, AMD provides a static breakdown of the major components of its non-GAAP operating loss adjustment, identifying stock-based compensation as a parallel driver to NVDA's compensation increases.

sentences.text: Operating expenses increased for fiscal year 2024, driven by growth in employees and compensation increases.
All Other operating loss of $4.2 billion in 2024 primarily consisted of $2.4 billion of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and $1.4 billion of stock-based compensation expense.
